a few t-storms mainly focused across western MA/CT. Light E/SE
winds.

t-storms moving across SNE. Variable winds, mostly e/SE across
eastern New Eng and shifting to N in the CT valley.

vsby potentially down to 1/4SM at times. Should see the fog
burn off 12-13z, but cigs probably only improving to MVFR toward
midday before dropping back to IFR-LIFR by late in the
day/evening. Low confidence on exact timing.

news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /18Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...

Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

Through 00Z...High confidence in trends moderate in timing.

Mix of MVFR to IFR conditions across the region as the stratus
is still struggling to lift our and is actually starting to
already advect back in. On top of this have widespread scattered
showers and storms developing across the west and continuing
into the evening. Leaned toward the ARW guidance as it has been
doing okay based on latest obs. Think the thunder risk is
greatest for BAF/BDL and perhaps ORH this afternoon Winds out
of the S/SE at 5-10 kts.

Tonight...Moderate confidence.

IFR-LIFR stratus redevelops. Scattered to numerous showers with
embedded t-storms mainly focused across CT and western/central
MA. This activity may push into eastern areas toward the Mon AM
push. Light E/SE winds.

Monday...Moderate confidence.

MVFR-LIFR conditions with numerous showers and scattered
t-storms moving across SNE. Variable winds, mostly E/SE across
eastern New Eng and shifting to N in the CT valley.

Monday Night...Moderate confidence.

Gradual improvement from MVFR/IFR to VFR from south to north as
precipitation lifts to the north. May be more scattered/spotty
as drier air punches into the region. Variable winds shift to
the W/NW late as the low lifts into/through the region.

BOS Terminal...Moderate confidence. IFR conditions lowering to
LIFR with visby reductions toward 23-02Z. Rain showers with
embedded thunder possible toward the Mon AM push and through the
day. Have held off on a thunder mention at this point. May
slowly improve to IFR on Monday.

BDL Terminal...Moderate confidence. MVFR conditions lowering to
IFR with showers and thunderstorms. Thunderstorm activity
fairly widespread this afternoon, but may downtick a bit during
the 03-06Z window and become more embedded in nature. Numerous
showers especially earlier on Mon with embedded thunderstorms.
Could see improvement to MVFR by the afternoon.

Outlook /Tuesday through Thursday/...

Tuesday: VFR. Breezy. Chance SHRA, isolated TSRA.

Tuesday Night: VFR.

Wednesday: VFR. Breezy.

Wednesday Night: VFR.

Thursday: VFR. Breezy. Chance SHRA, isolated TSRA.

news.text:
.AVIATION /16Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Forecast Confidence
Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

12Z Update...

Today... High confidence in trends, moderate in timing

Overnight fog/IFR conditions that developed across the
south coast and Islands overnight will lift to MVFR, MVFR/IFR
elsewhere with widespread drenching showers and thunderstorms.
Conditions this morning, between 12-16Z, look particularly poor
for western terminals with the possibility of a near stationary
convective line forming near or along the I-84 corridor. Variety
of TSRA and VCTS used at most terminals today, with the
exception of the Cape and Islands. Heavy rain/thunderstorm
threat begins to shift east after ~20Z. Gusty south/southwest
winds possible, up to 20-30kt possible.

Tonight...Moderate confidence in timing

Downpours and thunderstorms taper off from west to east, with
most terminals free of rain by 06Z, though some showers may
linger across the Cape until 09Z. IFR/MVFR to begin the evening,
lifting to MVFR/VFR by daybreak. A few thunderstorms possible
overnight but confidence on coverage is much less after 00Z,
thus, elected to leave out of the TAF. Winds shifting from the
S/SW to the WSW as cold front approaches from the west.

Monday... High confidence

Lingering MVFR along the eastern MA coastline and Cape through
15Z, otherwise VFR with clearing skies. Light westerly winds
shift to the SW by afternoon.

KBOS TAF...High confidence in trends, moderate in timing.

Shower activity becoming more widespread Sun AM with embedded
thunder mid AM into the afternoon as a line of showers/storms
moves in. Could see briefly higher gusts/heavy downpours if the
line moves over the terminal. Still could have some thunder
during the afternoon, but coverage appearing more spotty in
nature. MVFR develops overnight, VFR possible by 12Z.

KBDL TAF...High confidence in trends, moderate in timing.

MVFR to IFR, heavy downpours and thunderstorms develop after
10Z this morning, becoming more widespread through 16Z as a near
stationary convective line develops somewhere in the vicinity
of BDL. Rain and thunderstorms expected all day, gradually
deteriorating after 00Z tonight. MVFR improving to VFR by
daybreak with a windshift to the west; 5-10kt.

chance TSRA.

Tuesday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA, isolated TSRA.

06Z Update:

Through Today... High Confidence in trends, moderate in timing

Widely scattered showers across the interior through 12Z with a
secondary surge of downpours and convection across the Cape and
Islands between 08-12Z, otherwise, dry for most terminals
through daybreak. Fog that formed overnight will burn off
with daytime heating at inland terminals, but may hang around at
coastal terminals through 15-16Z. Thus, IFR improving to
MVFR/VFR, lowest on the Cape and Islands, through 16Z, VFR
thereafter. Generally light SW winds become W by mid morning,
except on the Cape where S winds prevail for a good portion of
the day. Winds generally less than 10kt, but some gusts possible
for ACK/HYA/FMH.

Tonight... High Confidence

VFR becoming IFR, first along the south coast, Cape, and Islands
as early as 23Z, MVFR/IFR overspreads much of the area as
stratus before fog develops after midnight. Winds less than 10kt
shifting back to the S/SW overnight.

Tuesday... Moderate Confidence in coverage of Tstorms

Fog burns off once again during the early daylight hours, with
IFR becoming VFR. Mainly dry until the late afternoon when a
front brings the chance for showers/downpours/isolated
thunderstorms to western terminals of ORE/BAF/BDL. Shower
chances also increase across the Cape and Islands after 22Z,
leaving a mainly dry slot across Central and Eastern MA and RI.
Winds generally light thanks to an inversion, 5-10kt.

KBOS TAF...Moderate confidence. IFR gradually becoming VFR
through 15Z. VFR after. Light SW winds before sunrise become W
around 16Z, near 10kt. Fog possible again after 06Z this
evening.

KBDL TAF...Moderate confidence. IFR becoming VFR quickly after
12Z. Mainly dry with W winds less than 10 kt. Downpour/ t-storm
chances increase after 20Z Tuesday due to approaching cold
front. Confidence too low to include in TAF at this time.

Tuesday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA, isolated TSRA.

news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /06Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

Through this Morning: High confidence in trends, but only
moderate confidence on timing.

IFR-LIFR with widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms.
While this threat looks greatest during the early morning
towards the south coast. Categories are still expected to be
mainly in the IFR-LIFR range until we get to this aftn. SE
winds 5-10 kt should shift to S/SSW upon passage of warm front.

This Afternoon: Moderate confidence.

Expecting to see some breaks in clouds/improvement in flight
categories toward MVFR levels. Couldn't rule out a rogue SHRA or
TS during the early afternoon, but think better chances for
+SHRA/TSRA arrive after 21Z or so for the western airports
associated with the approach of a cold front. These storms may
become strong and produce gusty winds, frequent lightning and
heavy downpours reducing visibility.

Tonight: High confidence.

SCT TSRA, some strong to start, should advance eastward off the
Berkshires/CT Valley and weaken as they move east between 01-03z
Tue. MVFR/IFR to start, but should see rapid improvement to VFR
upon passage of this cold front. It may take until later tonight
or early Tue before we see VFR categories for eastern airports.

Tuesday: High confidence.

Becoming VFR.

KBOS TAF...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact timing.

KBDL TAF...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact timing.

Outlook /Tuesday Night through Friday/...

.AVIATION /18Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

18Z TAF Update

Moderate confidence.

Mix of VFR and MVFR across the area (with localized IFR
underneath the heaviest rain areas), and that will be the case
for the rest of the afternoon. SHRA and TSRA will develop, with
an expected broken line of thunderstorms forming to our west
and then moving across southern New England between roughly
21z-02z. The thunderstorms will be weakening as they move east,
and especially as we reach sunset. Did the best to time the
potential via TEMPO groups, but there are errors of 1 to 2 hours
either side of what the TAFs show. That is the nature of trying
to time convection before it really fully develops.

TSRA/SHRA dissipate by 04z. Should see widespread MVFR/IFR
ceilings and some light fog develop. A front will move through
late tonight, producing a wind shift to the west/northwest.

Drier air starts to move in Tuesday morning, so we should see
conditions improve to VFR area wide by 15z. NW surface winds may
gust 15-20kt by late morning in many areas. VFR conditions
expected to continue into Tuesday night.

KBOS TAF...Moderate confidence. Whether or not TSRA impact BOS
will be related to the timing of the line coming through early
this evening. The earlier the arrival, the higher the liklihood
of TSRA. MVFR conditions late this evening, should transition to
a period of IFR ceilings after midnight. Winds veering to the
west/northwest will result in VFR conditions developing Tuesday
morning.

KBDL TAF...Moderate confidence. Could be several SHRA/TSRA that
impact the terminal through 22z. Potential could continue
through 00z.

Outlook /Tuesday Night through Friday/...

VFR.

06z TAF Update...

Today and tonight...Moderate Confidence.

IFR/LIFR conditions in low clouds and areas of fog are they main
story very early this morning. We should see the low clouds and
fog dissipate after sunrise...although this process will
probably be somewhat slower in spots especially in the CT River
Valley as well as the Cape/Islands.

After the low clouds and fog burn off we should see a period of
mainly VFR conditions later this morning into a good portion of
the afternoon. Precipitation should then overspread the region
from west to east between 20z and 23z. Conditions should lower
to MVFR/IFR levels. Ptype will mainly be snow NW of I-95...but
a period of rain may occur near and especially southeast of
I-95. Ptype should transition to mainly snow northwest of the
Cape Cod Canal by 00z/01z or so. The heaviest of the snow will
likely occur through 04z/05z when IFR/LIFR conditions are
expected. Snowfall rates of 1-2" per hour will be possible at
times. Total snow accumulations of 3-6"/4-8" will be common for
much of the region northwest of the Cape Cod Canal. Ptype
probably changes to all snow before ending even across the Cape.
The last of the steady snow should exit the coast by 09z/10z
Mon. Conditions will improve to VFR by daybreak Monday.

Winds should become N at 5 to 10 knots today by afternoon. The
winds will then become more NW later tonight with gusts of 20-25
knots developing and perhaps up to 30 knots in a few of the
typical spots.

Monday...High Confidence.

Mainly VFR outside a few brief spot snow showers that will be
possible. NW wind gusts of 20 to 30 knots.

roughly between 00z and 05z. 1" per hour snowfall rates possible
at times.

news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /21Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

Rest of Today:

Snow and sleet have mostly ended with just rain showers with
freezing rain in isolated spots in the high terrain. IFR/LIFR
CIGS continue through the afternoon. Wind shear picks up from
the SW this afternoon, especially near coastal areas. Winds
over the Cape and the Islands could briefly become very gusty
out of the SW late this afternoon to early this evening at 40-50
knots.

Tonight:

Cold front sweeps the remaining precip and IFR CIGS offshore
this evening from west to east between 23z-02z. CIGS quickly pop
up to MVFR then VFR. Winds turn west and become gusty around
30-40 knots.

Sunday:

VFR and very windy. Winds gusting 40-50 knots, possibly up to 60
knots in the elevated terrain and near the Cape and Islands.

Sunday Night:

VFR. Winds remain strong out of the west at 35-45 knots.

KBOS TAF...Moderate Confidence

IFR/LIFR. Periods of moderate to heavy rain this afternoon.
Wind shear from the SW increase this afternoon to 40-60 knots.
Cold front moves through around 01z lifting CIGS back to VFR and
drying out any remaining rain showers. Very windy behind the
cold front with west winds gusting 40-50 knots through Monday
night.

KBDL TAF...Moderate confidence .

IFR/LIFR. Periods of moderate to heavy rain this afternoon.
Wind shear from the SW increase this afternoon to 30-50 knots.
Cold front moves through around 23z lifting CIGS back to VFR and
drying out any remaining rain showers. Very windy behind the
cold front with west winds gusting 40-50knots through Monday
night.

Outlook /Tuesday through Friday/...

Tuesday: VFR. Windy with gusts up to 35 kt.

Tuesday Night: VFR. Windy with gusts up to 30 kt.

Wednesday: VFR. Breezy.

Wednesday Night: VFR. Slight chance SN.

Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Breezy. Chance
SN.

Thursday Night: VFR. Breezy. Chance SN.

Friday: VFR. Breezy.

news.speaker: NWS New York forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /15Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
A frontal boundary will remain in the vicinity of the terminals
today and tonight.

A brief period of dry conditions this afternoon before another
chance of showers and thunderstorms redevelop for the late
afternoon into the evening. Confidence of timing and placement
of any showers remains low. Will include a TEMPO from about
20-24z for a TSRA, where highest confidence is thunder
development.

Categories of flight categories at any one terminal is low and
could vary VFR to MVFR depending on where the showers and
thunderstorms have occurred or will occur. Additional sub-VFR
conditions in showers and thunderstorms later this afternoon is
expected. Some of the outlying terminals may have MVFR or IFR
fog/stratus develop late tonight.

Winds of variable direction early this afternoon due to numerous
thunderstorm outflow boundaries however a return to S/SW flow
around 8-10 kt develops going into this afternoon. Winds become
light and variable once again late tonight into early Saturday
morning.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Low confidence with the timing of showers and thunderstorms
today. Low confidence of flight categories.

OUTLOOK FOR 12Z SATURDAY THROUGH TUESDAY...

Saturday: MVFR or lower possible in the morning, otherwise VFR
with a chance of showers/thunderstorms in the afternoon and
evening.

Sunday-Tuesday: Chance of showers/thunderstorms with MVFR or
lower.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

A frontal boundary will remain in the vicinity of the terminals
this morning. A cold front approaches this afternoon and moves
through the area tonight. Weak high pressure briefly builds in
late tonight.

region through this afternoon, with periods of moderate to heavy
rainfall. There is some uncertainty with the timing and
placement of the heavier/stronger thunderstorms, some of which
could produce gusty winds. Conditions will be mainly IFR with
periods of MVFR possible. Thunderstorms and then showers end
mid to late afternoon into tonight west to east. Again, there
are timing uncertainties with the ending of thunderstorms and

.AVIATION /09Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
*Significant winter storm to impact the terminals Tuesday.

Low pressure approaches from the southwest overnight, passing south
of the area towards midday, before moving away late in the afternoon
and evening.

Precip will be mainly snow at the start for northern most terminals,
with a brief period of rain or a rain/snow mix at the more southern
terminals. Precip then changes to all snow with IFR conditions for
the more southern terminals by 10-12z. A low end chance remains that
some ice pellets mix in during the transition from rain to snow, but
confidence of occurrence is not high enough and duration not long
enough to warrant including in the TAF. Snow then continues through
the early afternoon, and will be heavy at times during the morning
with VLIFR visibilities. The snow tapers in the afternoon, with dry
conditions and VFR returning by late afternoon.

The winds increase into the morning push, and will probably be
strongest towards the tail end, or just after the AM push, with
sustained winds around 20kt and gusts around 30kt from 13z-17z from
the NE, then N. Winds back toward the NW late Tues aftn with gust
still 20-25kt. Gusts likely momentarily end Tue evening.

Forecast Airport Snowfall Totals:

KJFK/KLGA/KEWR/KTEB/KSWF: 5-8 inches

KISP/KHPN/KBDR/KGON: 6-10 inches

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Amendments will be needed for flight category changes and probably
precip type timing adjustments approaching the morning push. Precip
at onset may be all snow at some of the terminals instead of a
rain/snow mix or all rain.

OUTLOOK FOR 06Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY...

Tuesday night through Wednesday night...VFR. NW winds G20-25kt
during the nighttime and around 30kt daytime Wed.

Thursday night: Chance of MVFR and snow showers or mixed rain/snow
showers. NW winds G25kt late.

Friday: VFR. NW winds G25-30kt.

can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

news.text:
.AVIATION /00Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
A cold front will passes east of the terminals. High pressure
slowly builds in through Tuesday night.

Line of showers and thunderstorms will continue to progress
across Long Island and southeast CT terminals. This activity
should push east of KGON by 02z.

Mainly VFR through the TAF period. MVFR ceilings around 2.5-3kft
are expected tonight. However, this could just remain scattered
with VFR prevailing.

Winds will continue to shift to the WNW-NW this evening behind
the cold front passage. Sustained speeds around 10 kt with gusts
15-20 kt are expected this evening. Gusts likely drop off
03-05z. NW winds increase after day break and should be 10-15kt
with gusts around 20 kt on Tuesday. The gusts could end up
occasional. Any gusts likely end Tuesday evening.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
Gusts this evening and on Tuesday may be occasional.

MVFR ceilings around 030 overnight may end up SCT or not
prevail. may end up SCT.

OUTLOOK FOR 00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY...

Tuesday Night: A gust G15-20kt possible in the evening. VFR.

.AVIATION /09Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
A cold front will approach this afternoon and move across the area
this evening and overnight.

Mainly VFR. LIFR or lower conditions will impact KGON and KISP
this morning. There is also a chance that some lower conditions
could get into KBDR with a lower chance at KJFK.

SW winds may go light and variable for a few hours, before veering
NW toward daybreak, then backing SW once again into late morning.
Speeds increase to 10 kt, with gusts toward 20 kt possible after
18Z, though may be more occasional at some sites. Risk for TSRA late
afternoon and early eve, mainly 20Z to 00Z Fri. Any TSRA could
produce brief IFR conditions. Drier and VFR conditions expected
tonight.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Can not rule out low cigs reaching KJFK early this morning.

Gusts 20 kt possible this afternoon, may be more occasional.

Timing of TSRA may be off by an hour or two.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z FRIDAY THROUGH MONDAY...

Thursday night: VFR conditions.

Friday: VFR. NW winds G15-18kt.

Saturday through Monday: VFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

.AVIATION /06Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
A stationary frontal boundary remains near the terminals through
tonight.

Mainly VFR to start with a complex of showers and thunderstorms
mainly impacting Long Island and southeast CT terminals through
09z. Additional showers are possible elsewhere through much of
the morning hours. IFR or even LIFR is possible at KISP and
KGON. MVFR is otherwise expected around day break, but
confidence in it prevailing is low so have gone with tempos at
most sites except east of the NYC metros.

VFR is anticipated this afternoon with a chance of showers and
thunderstorms. Have left the PROB30 in place for NYC metro and
Lower Hudson Valley terminals this afternoon and early evening.
Coverage however may end up more isolated. Conditions should
lower tonight with MVFR most sites and IFR or LIFR possible east
of the NYC metro terminals.

Mainly light winds this morning. A light W or SW flow may
develop at NYC terminals after day break but winds should
gradually become S-SE late morning into the afternoon remaining
under 10 kt.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...
TSRA expected to stay east early this morning.

MVFR may prevail this morning and could linger a few hours
longer than in TAF this afternoon.

Some variability in wind direction is possible throughout the
TAF period as wind speeds will overall be light.

Amendments likely to refine the timing of showers and
thunderstorms this afternoon and evening.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z FRIDAY THROUGH MONDAY...

Thursday night: MVFR or lower possible.

Friday - Sunday: VFR. A chance of showers and thunderstorms
during the afternoon and early evening near and northwest of the
NYC terminals with MVFR possible.

Monday: VFR. A chance of showers and thunderstorms with MVFR
possible.

can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

afternoon. Eastern areas such as KGON and KISP may only improve

could occur earlier than this. Visibilities may also come down,
late tonight, with lower visibilities across the aforementioned
eastern terminals. there is a great deal of uncertainty with
the ceiling and visibility forecast through the period.

SE winds today at around 10 kt. There may be isolated gusts to
around 15 kt during the late morning into the afternoon.

the forecast period.

becoming VFR thereafter, except MVFR or lower in any showers
and thunderstorms that move through in the afternoon and
overnight.

Tuesday-Thursday: Mainly VFR. Showers or
thunderstorm possible in the afternoon and evening.

A weak cold front remains over the region through Tuesday.

A fair amount of uncertainty in the flight category forecast
overnight as conditions may vary from IFR (mainly for eastern
terminals) to VFR (across city terminals, with brief IFR to
MVFR) tonight. Add to that the saturated ground from the heavy
rain yesterday, which may aid in development of fog across NE
NJ. The question is whether this will advect or develop over the
city terminals as the night progresses. VFR for Tuesday into
Tuesday night outside any possible showers/tstms.

Light and variable winds overnight, becoming S-SSW 5-10kt
Tuesday.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Amendments expected with overall low confidence in flight
category forecast tonight/early Tuesday morning. MVFR could
prevail all night with brief IFR possible.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY...

Tuesday Night: VFR during the afternoon/evening with a chance
of a shower/thunderstorm. MVFR or lower possible, especially
east of NYC metro at night.

Wednesday-Friday: MVFR or lower in any afternoon/evening
showers/thunderstorms.

Saturday: Mainly VFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

A weak cold front remains over the region through tonight.

MVFR to VFR conditions are expected to improve to VFR for most
terminals this morning. Metro terminals are expected to remain
VFR through the forecast period, though there is a low chance of
MVFR conditions moving in late tonight, with a low to medium
chance for KJFK. Outlying terminals have a good chance of seeing
MVFR to IFR conditions tonight, with a low chance of LIFR
possible.

Light and variable winds this morning become S-SSW 10 kt or
less.

news.text:
.AVIATION /15Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
High pressure builds into the area today and exits offshore
Sunday.

Expecting mainly VFR conditions through the TAF period. There is
a slight chance of a rain shower this afternoon into early
evening, mainly north of the NYC terminals.

Winds will transition from NW or variable this morning hours to
a sea breeze this afternoon for some terminals, changing wind
direction to more southerly, while remaining more westerly for
others in the afternoon. Wind speeds remain near 5-10 kt much of
the TAF period. There will be a time period in the afternoon
when winds will be around 10 kt with some gusts up to 15-20 kt.
These wind gusts will subside by early evening as winds
transition to more westerly to southwesterly flow near 5-8 kt.
Once again, winds for some terminals away from NYC will have
wind speeds less than 5 kts with variable direction late
tonight.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

KJFK and KLGA sea breeze timing could be off by 1-2 hours.

KEWR low chance for sea breeze early evening with NW winds
prevailing at KTEB.

Some gusts 15-20 kt possible in the afternoon for KJFK.

OUTLOOK FOR 12Z SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY...

Sunday: VFR. Potential sea breeze enhancement at KJFK late in
the afternoon with southerly winds increasing to 15-20 kt.

Sunday night: Chance of showers and MVFR. Southerly wind gusts
15-20 kt for some coastal terminals.

Monday: Showers and MVFR. Slight chance of thunderstorms
afternoon into evening. SE gusts 20-25 kt during the day. SE-S
gusts 15-20 kt in the evening.

Tuesday: Chance of showers. MVFR possible.

Wednesday: Chance of showers. Slight chance of thunderstorms, mainly
in the afternoon into early evening. MVFR possible. SW wind
gusts 15-20 kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

.AVIATION /07Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
High pressure builds over the region overnight and moves east
of the area Sunday. Low pressure approaches Sunday night.

Lingering surface trough will make for potential for a few rain
showers from time to time during the TAF period, making for
possible brief MVFR conditions. Generally, more western areas
will have relatively higher chances for showers compared to
eastern areas.

However, mainly VFR conditions are anticipated through the TAF
period. Winds will be mainly southerly for much of the coastal
terminals around 5 kts overnight and then will increase to near 10-
13 kt Sunday late morning into the afternoon with some gusts up to
20 kt. Southerly winds decrease to 5-10 kts with gusts subsiding
Sunday night.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Start and end of gusts could be off by a few hours.

MVFR possible with some showers.

OUTLOOK FOR 06Z MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY...

Late Sunday night: Chance of showers towards daybreak Monday with
possible MVFR.

Monday: Showers and MVFR. Slight chance of a thunderstorm. SE wind
gusts 20-25 kt daytime and S-SW wind gusts near 20 kt for the
evening.

Tuesday: Slight chance to chance of showers. MVFR possible at times.

Wednesday: Shower chances increase, becomingly likely for western
areas. Slight chance to chance of thunderstorms for much of the area
afternoon into early evening. MVFR possible at times. SW wind gusts
15-20 kt.

Thursday: Mainly VFR. Chance of rain showers and MVFR possible.

can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

.AVIATION /12Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
A frontal boundary stalls near the region this morning before slowly
lifting back NE as a warm front this evening and tonight.

Varying flight categories early this morning with MVFR to IFR for
some Lower Hudson Valley and coastal CT terminals. VFR conditions
continue to prevail for NYC metro and Long Island terminals.

Confidence remains low with the exact timing when ceilings will
lower for the NYC and Long Island terminals. It appears more likely
to occur after 12z. A wintry mix inland and CT coast with some
spotty light rain towards NYC metro and Long Island. Sleet could
briefly mix in down towards the NYC metro. Any precip should become
spotty after 12z.

Rain will overspread the region late this afternoon and evening with
conditions becoming IFR. LIFR conditions are possible tonight.

A light NE flow early this morning will gradually veer to E and SE
through this evening. Winds will shift towards the S and SW once the
warm front lifts to the north overnight.

     NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Amendments expected for timing of flight category changes through
the TAF period.

Sleet could briefly mix in with any spotty light rain through day
break.

The afternoon KJFK, KLGA, and KEWR haze potential forecast is
YELLOW...which implies slant range visibility 4-6SM outside of cloud.

OUTLOOK FOR 06Z THURSDAY THROUGH SUNDAY...

Tonight-Thursday Night...Mainly IFR with periods of rain.

Friday...Chance of MVFR/IFR/rain AM. Improvement to VFR by afternoon.

Saturday...Mainly VFR. MVFR or lower developing in rain at night.

Sunday...MVFR or lower in rain. E-NE G20-25kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

evening. Winds will eventually shift towards the S and SW as

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...

Through 00Z...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact
timing.

MVFR for most with spotty IFR. VFR across the Cape/Islands at
the moment, but will see a return to MVFR as showers spread in.
There is a bit of a lull in the strong S winds, but will see
another surge of the low level jet between 20-00Z bringing a
return of 40-50 kt gusts across eastern areas into the evening.
Winds will be shifting to the SW/WSW as a strong cold front
swings through with gusts of 35-45+ kts. Precipitation ending
from west to east mid to late this afternoon and there could be
a touch of snow to wrap things up, but should not accumulate
outside of the higher terrain. There is a lower probability for
western airports (mainly BDL-BAF) where any wet pavement could
freeze and become icy as temperatures plummet heading into this
evening. Further east this risk should be mitigated by the
surge of strong winds, but any spots where there is standing
water could become icy.

Tonight...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact timing.

Improving to VFR for most outside of the Cape/Islands. Will have
MVFR conditions linger with ocean-effect snow showers. Most
likely at ACK, but could leak into HYA/FMH from time to time. Up
to an inch of accumulation is possible at ACK. WSW/SW winds at
15-25 kts with gusts of 35-45 kts in the evening. Gusts ease to
25-35 kts after 06Z.

Saturday and Saturday night...High confidence.

VFR for most, but MVFR/borderline MVFR conditions linger across
the Cape/Islands due to ocean effect snow showers. Will remain
gusty out of the SW/WSW with speeds of 15-20 kts and gusts of
25-35 kts. Winds ease to 5-10 kts Saturday night with gusts of
15-25 kts. The highest gusts confined to the Cape/Islands.
Could see another 1-2 inches of new snow across ACK.

KBOS Terminal...High confidence in trends, moderate in exact
timing of strongest winds this afternoon/evening.

KBDL Terminal...High confidence.

Outlook /Christmas Day through Tuesday/...

Christmas Day: VFR. Windy with local gusts up to 30 kt.

Sunday Night through Monday: VFR. Breezy.

Monday Night through Tuesday: VFR.

news.text:
.AVIATION /08Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Medium - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

06z TAF Update:

Rest of the Overnight: High confidence in trends, but low to
moderate confidence on both shower/storm coverage and timing.

LIFR with stratus and fog (VLIFR fog Cape and Islands/closer to
IFR- LIFR inland) for most airports S/E of I-95. North and west
of here, general trend is for deterioration, though the timing
isn't certain. Stratus likely to expand north in coverage from
ORH- PVD- PYM line thru ~08-11z at IFR to LIFR levels towards
BOS- BED. VFR for BDL and BED but MVFR type stratus bases should
develop around 09-11z. In addition, SHRA/isolated TS developing
over the waters may threaten at least FMH, HYA and ACK toward
daybreak. SE/S winds 4-8 kt.

Today: Moderate confidence.

Any stratus west of ORH should dissipate to BKN VFR ceilings by
13-14z. Stratus may improve to MVFR-VFR decks along a roughly similar
timeline into BOS/BED and PVD too. Timing of any improvement in
LIFR stratus and fog on Cape Cod and the Islands is uncertain,
and it is likely that fog or stratus will at least linger in
the nearshore waters much of the day.

Should see scattered to numerous showers and scattered storms
develop near and west of ORH today. Indicated PROB30 TSRA for
now but storms may develop as early as 15-17z. Less of a
shower/storm risk in eastern MA ad RI but chances increase after
18z, but left these airports at VCSH. Any storm may bring IFR
to LIFR visby heavy downpours with a direct hit, along with
cloud to ground lightning and brief strong wind gusts. SE/S
winds around 5-10 kt.

Tonight: High confidence in trends but low to moderate
confidence on storm chances and timing.

Deteriorating conditions to IFR-LIFR again with stratus and
locally dense fog with best chance for dense fog near the south
coast. We need to watch for overnight strong TS moving in from
southern NY/NJ, but the timing and how strong/if it maintains
itself are far from certain at this point in time. Current best
estimate for arrival into our western airports would be after
03z. SE to S winds 4-8 kt.

Tuesday: Moderate confidence, but low confidence on timing
shower/storm chances.

LIFR-IFR should lift and/or move offshore by mid morning. Our
weather pattern favors several opportunites for showers and
t-storms on Tuesday but given the potential for overnight
storms Monday night, when any storms develop Tuesday is highly
uncertain. SE to S winds 4-8 kt.

BOS Terminal...High confidence in trends, moderate on timing.
Deterioration to IFR-LIFR stratus ~08-11z and should scatter by
~14-16z. Better risk for TS west of BOS but chances increase
after 18z. Likely that categories go down to IFR/LIFR levels
again tonight.

BDL Terminal...High confidence in trends, moderate on timing.
Deterioration to MVFR and perhaps IFR ceilings ~08-11z.
Improvement by ~13-15z. PROB30 indicated for aftn TS, a few
could be strong with gusty winds, lightning and reduced visby
from heavy rain.

Medium - 30 to 60 percent.

Today...Moderate confidence.

14-16Z. Stratus may improve to MVFR-VFR decks along a roughly
similar timeline into BOS/BED and PVD too. Timing of any
improvement in LIFR stratus and fog on Cape Cod and the Islands
is uncertain, and it is likely that fog or stratus will at least
linger in the nearshore waters much of the day. Could perhaps
see some BKN IFR/LIFR conditions.

Should see scattered to numerous showers and scattered storms
develop near and west of ORH today. Indicated -SHRA and VCTS as
HREF guidance has good idea on thunder timing. Still could see
storms develop as early as 15-17Z. Less of a shower/storm risk
in eastern MA ad RI but chances increase after 18-20Z, but left
these airports at VCSH. Any storm may bring IFR to LIFR visby
heavy downpours with a direct hit. SE/S winds around 5-10 kt.

Tonight...High confidence in trends but low to moderate
confidence on storm chances and timing.

Deteriorating conditions to IFR-LIFR again with stratus and
locally dense fog with best chance for dense fog near the south
coast. We need to watch for overnight strong TS moving in from
southern NY/NJ, but the timing and how strong/if it maintains
itself are far from certain at this point in time. Current best
estimate for arrival into our western airports would be after
03Z. Have indicated this risk with a PROB30 across interior
terminals. SE to S winds 4-8 kt.

Tuesday...Moderate confidence, but low confidence on timing
shower/storm chances.

weather pattern favors several opportunities for showers and
t-storms on Tuesday but given the potential for overnight
storms Monday night, when any storms develop Tuesday is highly
uncertain. SE to S winds 4-8 kt.

1.5-3 kft around 14-16Z. Better risk for TS west of BOS but

to IFR/LIFR levels again tonight.

tonight.

thunderstorm winds, torrential rainfall capable of temporary

to as much as 50 kt. Anticipate SW gusts 25-35 kt this
afternoon with the higher ends of gusts toward the Cape/Islands.

gives way to VFR conditions for most. Will have to watch for

daybreak.

could be strong.

deteriorate in afternoon to early evening.

news.text:
.AVIATION /15Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

Overnight Through Today: High confidence.

Active aviation weather in this period with IFR-LIFR ceilings,
VFR to IFR visibility moderate to heavy rains, strong winds and
low- level wind shear/turbulence.

Ceilings trend IFR to LIFR overnight into early Mon AM as rain
moves northward. Visibilities in rain thru about 10z should stay
3-6 SM with intervals of mist at times. Rain ramps up to steady
moderate to heavy-intensity with IFR visibilities in western
MA/CT airports, then around 12-16z for eastern airports. There
may be rumble or two of thunder near the southeast MA/RI coast.

SE winds to continue to increase in the 09-18z timeframe, with
peak gusts 35-45 kt in the interior, 45-50 kt in the I-95
BOS/PVD corridor airports, and 55 kt Cape and Islands. Low level
jet of 60-80 kt could support areas of turbulence, although
surface winds are likely to be gusty. Winds then shift to SW to
WSW 19-00z with a rapid decrease in gusts to 25-35 kt and
improving ceilings/visibilities to MVFR with that windshift.

Tonight: Moderate to high confidence.

SCT-BKN VFR to MVFR ceilings with better chance at MVFR bases
near the higher terrain. There may be returning MVFR bases over
Cape Cod and Islands as passing secondary wave of low pressure
brushes our southeast outer waters. WSW gusts 25-35 kt
initially, strongest over SE MA/RI/Cape and Islands although
gust speeds decrease a bit to around 20-25 kt thru overnight.

Tuesday: Moderate to high confidence.

Continued SCT-BKN VFR to MVFR bases, though may trend OVC in
the western higher terrain. Could see isolated -SHRA, or -SHSN
in the higher terrain, although drier weather should prevail
most of the time. W to WNW speeds 10-14 kt with gusts 22-23 kt.

KBOS TAF...High confidence in TAF.

MVFR trending to IFR early this morning. 4-6 SM rain showers
trend to an IFR moderate to heavy rain after 13z. Moderate to
heavy rain begins late overnight and lasts through tomorrow
morning. Wind shear of 40-60 knots is possible starting this
evening through tomorrow afternoon. SE winds increase into the
morning, peaking between 15-19z with gusts up to 50 knots. After
19z Monday, winds begin to diminish and ceilings improve to
MVFR.

KBDL TAF...High confidence in TAF.

MVFR to IFR early this morning. Steady light rain becomes heavy
rain with gusty winds to 45 knots through 18z tomorrow. After
18z, should see improvements to MVFR and gusty WSW winds.

Outlook /Tuesday Night through Friday/...

Tuesday Night through Wednesday: VFR. Breezy.

Wednesday Night through Thursday Night: VFR. Windy with gusts
up to 35 kt.

Friday: VFR. Windy with local gusts up to 30 kt.

.AVIATION /03Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

0230z update...Line of showers with embedded thunderstorms over
RI and southeast MA continues to show signs of weakening per
radar trends and warming cloud tops. Will have to watch cluster
of convection over NJ, as this activity may clip the south coast
and islands overnight. Otherwise, gusty SW winds continue across
southeast MA given low level jet of up to 50 kt at 2-3kft from
the southwest. Earlier discussion below.

================================================================

Tonight...Moderate confidence.

Thunderstorms weaken into showers after 00z with drying
conditions after 06z. Low end MVFR to IFR conditions across much
of the region. Light to moderate rain and possibly a rumble of
thunder across the Cape and Islands after 06z tonight. SW winds
remain elevated at 15 to 25 knots along with continued wind
shear over the Cape and Islands with 50-60 knots LLJ.

Monday...High confidence.

IFR/MVFR CIGS lift to VFR region wide in the mid to late
morning. Winds turn west at 10-15 knots in the afternoon.
Interior terminals may see weak showers in the afternoon
through sunset.

KBOS TAF...Moderate confidence in TAF

VFR this afternoon with gusty SW winds up to 25 knots. Chance
for thunderstorms this evening between 23-01z, with showers
possibly lingering to 06z. IFR to low end MVFR tonight, lifting
to VFR tomorrow morning after 12z-14z. Winds turn west in the
afternoon at 10-15 knots. Low chance for weak showers tomorrow
afternoon

KBDL TAF...Moderate confidence in TAF

VFR this afternoon with a chance for thunderstorms this mainly
between 22z-00z. MVFR to VFR tonight. VFR tomorrow with
scattered light showers in the afternoon and gusty west winds.

news.speaker: NWS Boston forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /07Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...

Forecast Confidence Levels:

Low - less than 30 percent.
Moderate - 30 to 60 percent.
High - greater than 60 percent.

Through 12Z...Moderate confidence.

Will have MVFR to LIFR conditions with LIFR most likely across
the immediate south coast. Most of the showers are not impacting
visibility. Think that activity across interior will remain
generally as showers/weaken, but cannot completely rule a few
rumbles of thunder. Best shot for thunder comes across the
immediate south coast as we head toward daybreak as dewpoints
climb and the LLJ intensifies. Have tried to highlight this for
PVD-FMH-HYA and ACK with a VCTS. Winds out of the S to SW
at 10-15 kts with gusts of 20-30 kts.

Today...Moderate confidence.

Conditions improve to VFR for most by roughly 13-16Z. The only
exception is for PVD-OWD where MVFR to LIFR stratus lingers.
May have a few showers/storms exiting the Cape and Islands
during this timeframe.

Another round of showers/storms expected to materialize roughly
17-19Z across the interior. These will push southeastward toward
the south coast by the evening. Strong to severe storms
possible, which if impacting a terminal would bring the risk of
damaging wind gusts and conditions briefly deteriorating to MVFR
to LIFR. Have handled this risk with a PROB30 for all terminals,
except across the south coast where am uncertain on how quickly
the line weakens given the stable boundary layer as the marine
layer will be in place. For now utilized a VCTS for this. Will
have SW winds at 101-5 kts with gusts of 20-30 kts. Winds
shifting to the W/WNW toward the evening across the interior.

Tonight...Moderate confidence.

MVFR to IFR with showers/t-storms in the evening along the
south coast, then improving to VFR overnight. Wind shift to NW
00-06Z. Speeds of 5-10 kts with gusts diminishing toward 03-06Z,
but will then increase to 15-20 kts toward daybreak.

Monday...High confidence.

VFR to start, but as CU develops will have borderline MVFR/VFR
cloud bases. Should see hit or miss showers/storms developing,
which could potentially produce some small hail. Winds out of
the NNW to N at 5-10 kts with gusts of 15-20 kts.

KBOS TAF...Moderate confidence in TAF.

Conditions MVFR to IFR through roughly 12Z. Could see a spot
shower heading into the AM push and perhaps a rumble of thunder.
Though confidence in the thunder was too low to include a
mention at this point. Will improve to VFR roughly 15-17Z.
Scattered showers/storms developing 19-23Z and could bring
strong to perhaps damaging winds and brief heavy downpours.
Improving to VFR as showers/storms move toward the south coast
by the evening. S to SW winds at 10-15 kts with 20-25 kt gusts.
Winds shifting to the W/WNW during the evening once the
showers/storms slide through.

KBDL TAF...Moderate confidence in TAF.

MVFR to IFR conditions as we head into the AM push today. Should
gradually improve to VFR by 14-16Z. Cannot rule out a spot
shower. Will have increasing chances of showers/storms this
afternoon/evening, some of which could bring strong to perhaps
damaging wind gusts. Have handled with a PROB30 from 17-23Z.
These storms moves S/SE of the terminal during the evening and
will fairly quickly improve to VFR. Winds out of the S at 5-15
kts. Will shift to the W/WNW this evening in wake of
shower/storm activity. Could have some 15-20 kt gusts this
afternoon (not associated with the thunderstorms).

Outlook /Monday Night through Thursday/...

Monday Night through Tuesday Night: VFR.

Wednesday: VFR. Breezy.

Wednesday Night: VFR. Breezy. Slight chance SHRA.

Independence Day: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Breezy.
Slight chance SHRA.

terminals after 1530Z. MVFR to IFR conditions are expected until

thunderstorms then affect the Lower Hudson Valley terminals
possibly through 17-18Z. Some of the storms across the Lower
Hudson Valley could produce winds in excess of 40 kt, but for
now, only TEMPO 25 kt to 30 kt gusts. Hail is also possible,
mainly across KSWF through 17Z.

Another trough moves into the region later today along with a
warm front to the west.

VFR across the NYC terminals right now with some lingering
stratus and fog elsewhere. These conditions are expected to
improve over the next few hours. However, scattered showers and
thunderstorms this morning could bring conditions back down to
MVFR or lower.

morning before showers and thunderstorms return through the
evening. There is potential for stronger thunderstorms in the
late afternoon, especially from the NYC metro terminals and
north and west. Heavy rain, gusty winds and even small hail are
possible. MVFR/IFR likely with any thunderstorm. Only put TSRA
in a small window in the TAF when thunder is most likely, but
any activity today as the potential to produce lightning.

.AVIATION /00Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
A frontal system moves slowly eastward tonight through
Wednesday.

Currently an area of showers and thunderstorms was moving
through northeastern New Jersey, into the NYC metro terminals,
and into the lower Hudson Valley. Conditions mainly VFR with a
chance of MVFR in the showers and thunderstorms. Threat of
thunderstorms ends south soon after 00Z, and by 03Z at KSWF,
and maybe before 02Z. Showers will be possible east of the NYC
metro terminals late evening into late tonight. Scattered
showers are possible overnight, however probabilities too low,
and confidence in areas of showers too uncertain to keep chances
in the TAFs for an extended period of time. The best chances for
thunderstorms Wednesday will be mid to late afternoon, and kept
the PROB30 at this time.

MVFR to IFR stratus is expected to develop once again tonight,
with areal coverage and timing uncertain. However, LIFR is only
expected at KGON late tonight. Conditions rather quickly improve
to VFR Wednesday morning.

Winds S to SE become light and variable at most locations
tonight. The winds then have a more westerly component to them
towards daybreak and increase out of the W SW Wednesday morning.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Thunderstorms have weakened and a rumble/isolate storm remains
possible until around 01Z. There is uncertainty as to how far
west MVFR to IFR stratus will develop late evening, 04Z, and
overnight.

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
A weak stationary front in close proximity to the NYC and Lower
Hudson Valley terminals this morning will shift slowly west
today. A frontal wave over the Ohio Valley approaches on Sunday.

Plan to stay close to a persistence type of forecast as there
has been no change in the airmass or the flow regime across the
terminal forecast area. Thus, expect a mainly VFR forecast with
occasional MVFR/IFR during the early morning hours with
improvement after 12Z. Warm season fog/low clouds are often a
challenge and primarily hinge on warm, humid air moving across
the cooler nearshore waters. In addition, there is less
radiational cooling in this type of airmass. Bottom line, don't
see much change than what we have been dealing with the last

Offshore high pressure remains during the TAF period. An upper
level disturbance will move through the area along with some
showers and thunderstorms this afternoon into this evening
across. Timing is for a line of storms to move through after

strong gusts associated with these storms of up to 40 kt. If the
storms become severe, then gusts to 50 kt are possible, but
right now, there is a low chance of this happening. These storms
are forecast to weaken as they head east. Although uncertainty
is higher across ern terminals, prob30s have been converted to

terminals.

news.speaker: NWS New York forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
A warm front slowly approaches from SW today, likely lifting
across the terminals tonight.

Mainly MVFR this morning, but guidance has trended toward a
better chance for a period of VFR this afternoon. For the time,
this will be highlighted with a TEMPO group. The first round of
showers exits far eastern terminals by early this afternoon,
with an isolated shower or thunderstorm possible for the
remainder of the day.

Another round of showers and thunderstorms is expected tonight.
Have gone with a TEMPO for TSRA for the NYC and Lower Hudson
Valley terminals, mainly after 00Z. There is quite a bit of
uncertainty with the timing and extent of these showers and
thunderstorms and amendments are likely. Otherwise, MVFR-IFR
conditions are forecast for tonight.

SE winds increase to 10-15 kt with gusts 18-25 kt late morning
into the afternoon, strongest along the immediate coast. The
highest wind speeds and gusts should begin to subside this
evening. Winds will then veer to the SW late tonight at 10kt or
less.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Ceilings may vary between MVFR and VFR, especially during the

news.text:
.AVIATION /12Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Low pressure passes north of the area this morning, dragging a
cold front across the terminals.

Spotty showers and possibly a thunderstorm will impact the
terminals through the morning hours, mainly from NYC and points
east. The best chance for a thunderstorm will be at KGON due to
marginal instability available.

Occasional MVFR ceilings this morning, possibly IFR early,
before improving to VFR by late morning early afternoon.
Ceilings may vary back and forth during this time.

Winds will start S-SSE 5-10kt, even be light and variable
inland, then veer to the SW-W after 12Z, increasing to 15-20kt
with gusts 22-28kt by early afternoon. A few higher gusts to
around 30 kt possible. W-NW winds will then be slow to diminish
Tuesday night.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Amendments likely as ceilings vary from mainly VFR to at times
MVFR. There is a low chance of IFR conditions toward daybreak.

OUTLOOK FOR 06Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY...

Late Tuesday night through Wednesday: VFR. W wind gusts around
20 kt.

Thursday: VFR.

Thursday Night-Friday: Mainly VFR. Chance of showers and MVFR. A
slight chance of thunderstorms Friday afternoon.

Saturday: Mainly VFR. Slight chance of afternoon showers and
thunderstorms mainly for NYC north and west.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

news.speaker: NWS New York forecast discussion
news.text:
.AVIATION /15Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
A cold front approaches from the NW today, preceded by a prefrontal
trough. Both will make their way through the area in the afternoon
and through the evening.

VFR expected through this afternoon. MVFR or lower conditions are
likely with any showers and/or thunderstorms today and tonight. Best
chance of TSRA 20-23Z Friday at KSWF, 21-01Z across the city
terminals, and 23-02Z at the eastern terminals. There is a low
chance of earlier SHRA or TSRA for KSWF between 17-19Z. Heavy
rain and gusty winds possible in any TSRA, along with a chance
of hail. Timing of the stronger thunderstorms is uncertain and
has trended slightly later. SHRA continue tonight through 06Z.
Cigs may drop to MVFR or lower for a period before the Saturday
morning push.

S/SW winds 10-15kt today, with a few occasional gusts up to 20kt.
Stronger winds are possible in vicinity of TSRA this afternoon
and evening. Wind direction could also become tricky in the
afternoon as the pre-frontal trough moves into the area, and
winds may even become light and variable for a couple of hours.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

A line of SHRA with possible embedded TSRA may move past the
area 16-19Z, but should remain mainly to the north of the NYC
terminals.

The main band of showers and thunderstorms this afternoon and
evening could vary by 1-2 hours. There also could be a few
random showers and thunderstorms ahead of this main band in the
afternoon.

OUTLOOK FOR 12Z SATURDAY THROUGH TUESDAY...

Saturday through Tuesday: VFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts,
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

.AVIATION /18Z FRIDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
A pre frontal trough was moving into the lower Hudson Valley and
into northeastern New Jersey at 17Z with showers and an isolated
thunderstorm possible. A cold front will follow late this
afternoon through late tonight.

VFR expected outside of any showers and thunderstorms when MVFR
conditions are expected, with brief IFR possible in stronger
thunderstorms. Timing of the thunderstorms continues to trend
slightly later, with thunderstorms in the NYC metro area 21Z to
01Z, and to the east 23Z to 03Z. Stronger storms, with gusty
winds and small hail possible, will be more likely across the
lower Hudson Valley into northeastern New Jersey, and the NYC
terminals. A few showers will remain possible in the vicinity
of, and post frontal into late tonight.

S to SW winds ahead of the cold front may briefly become light
and variable in the vicinity of the pre frontal trough. Post
cold front winds shift to NW to N and become gusty. Overnight
gusts may be more occasional.

  NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Showers were moving across the terminals, with an isolated
thunderstorm possible, through 20Z.

More organized thunderstorms will become likely late afternoon
into this evening 22Z to 01Z. Timing has trended slightly
later, and that trend may continue. A stronger storm remains
possible with gusts up to 40kt and small hail possible.

OUTLOOK FOR 18Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY...

.AVIATION /00Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
The main band of showers and thunderstorms has worked east of
the NYC and Lower Hudson Valley terminals. The area will continue
to weaken and diminish in coverage while working across the
eastern terminals the next couple of hours. A band of light
showers will follow, but should be brief. Actual cold front
works from west to east across the area from around 04Z at KSWF
to 09Z at KGON.

Mainly a VFR forecast outside of any heavier showers. Winds will
go light and variable. There is small chance that some patchy
fog and a brief IFR/LIFR ceiling develops before northerly
winds increase behind the cold front. There is also a chance
for a few gusts 15-20kt behind the cold front, but that is more
likely after 12Z Saturday. Gusts diminish in the later afternoon
Saturday as high pressure works in from the Great Lakes.

  ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

A brief shower is possible the first half of the night. Northerly
wind gusts could develop sooner than forecast behind the cold
front overnight, but should not be frequent until late morning.

OUTLOOK FOR 00Z SUNDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY...

.AVIATION /07Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
A warm front will continue to lift northeast through the area
overnight. A pre-frontal trough will approach and settle nearby
today, followed by a cold front this evening.

Seeing LIFR cond attm at KISP/KHPN/KGON, with KJFK currently VFR
but right on the edge of those conditions, which should return
there overnight into the AM hours. MVFR at KEWR/KTEB/KSWF should
also expand to KLGA/KBDR overnight.

Diminishing area of light showers moving across attm. Expect dry
cond thereafter until at least midday, then two rounds of tstm
are possible. The first of these with the pre-frontal trough
should impact the Hudson Valley terminals from 17Z-19Z, the NYC
metros from about 18Z-20Z, and out east across Long Island/CT
from 19Z-21Z. The second round with the cold front should occur
from late afternoon into the evening, impacting the NYC metros
from 22Z-23Z until 02Z-03Z, once again about an hour earlier to
the NW and an hour or two later to the E. Stronger cells with
either round could produce strong W-NW winds, but have not yet
mentioned this explicitly in TAF's.

Outside of tstms, S-SW winds 5-10 kt should become more SW and
increase to 10-15 G20kt by afternoon. After cold fropa this
evening, winds shift NW around or just over 10 kt, with some
terminals gusting to 15-20 kt.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

KJFK currently VFR, but sitting on the edge of LIFR cond that
could expand back into the terminal airspace overnight into the
AM push. MVFR likely to return to KLGA as well.

Strong wind gusts possible with any tstm directly impacting the
terminals this afternoon into this evening.

OUTLOOK FOR 06Z MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY...

Late Sunday night: VFR. NW winds G15-20kt.

Monday through Wednesday: VFR.

Thursday: Possible MVFR or lower cond with any late day or
nighttime showers/tstms.

mid morning. Embedded thunderstorm possible with this activity.

continued scattered SHRA at times late this morning and early
afternoon over the NYC metro, NE NJ, and the LoHud. Eastern
terminals (KISP, KBDR, KGON) may remain mostly dry during this
time.

Heavier showers are possible in the afternoon and early evening, and
chances for TSRA increase in this window at NYC terminals, KHPN, and
KSWF, but timing and coverage is fairly uncertain. Another lull
likely develops by the evening hours, before coverage of
showers and possible thunderstorms return overnight, mainly
after 6Z Sat, with conditions potentially lowering toward IFR.

gradual improvement and return to VFR.

generally increasing to 10 kt. Gusts up to 20 kt will be

.AVIATION /12Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
A frontal boundary lingers near the terminals today before pushing
east tonight.

Pockets of MVFR/IFR this morning as showers push north and east
through the region. A thunderstorm or two is also possible, though
this threat appears rather isolated. Precip ends generally between
15Z and 18Z from west to east and conditions gradually return to VFR
by late afternoon. Possible fog or low stratus development overnight
could lead to restrictions, but confidence too low to include
in TAF at this time. Otherwise, VFR on Sunday.

Southerly with speeds generally at or under 10 kt through this
evening. Frontal passage overnight will cause flow to lighten before
a N direction is established into Sunday AM. Flow turns S or SW by
the afternoon, with speeds remaining light.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Low confidence in TSRA coverage later this morning.

Timing of category improvement could be off by a couple of hours.

Possible vsby/cig restrictions Sunday morning.

Late Tonight: VFR. Light and variable winds.

Sunday: VFR.

Monday through Wednesday: Mainly VFR. A chance of afternoon into
early evening showers and thunderstorms with MVFR possible.

.AVIATION /08Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
A cold front approaches from the west this afternoon.

Mainly dry conditions this morning with VFR conditions expected.
Another round of showers and thunderstorms are expected this
afternoon, this time with a better chance of impacting the NYC
terminals with the approach of a cold front. Will include TEMPOs to
cover the thunderstorm threat this afternoon. Expect MVFR or lower
possible in any storms, along with a threat of gusty winds and heavy
rainfall during any storms. While most of the shower/thunderstorm
activity ends after 02z, there will still be a chance of showers
later at night.

S-SW winds are expected to remain 10kt or less this morning. Winds
increase once again this afternoon to 10-15kt with occasional gusts
into the 20-25kt range during the afternoon. Winds diminish again
tonight to 10kt or less, and start to turn a bit more towards the
west especially late in the TAF period.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of convection this afternoon may be +/- an hour or so.
Potential that winds gust 40-50 kt in stronger thunderstorms.

Wednesday night: MVFR or lower in possible showers.

morning with MVFR possible, otherwise VFR.

forecast this afternoon, but still increasing to 10-15 kt with

this evening.

13 kt expected at KJFK, KISP, KBDR, and KGON this afternoon. Winds
may start to shift towards the W where the sea breeze has occurred
late in the afternoon before becoming NW this evening with the cold
front passage. Wind speeds weaken overnight and become light and
variable at most sites. NW winds increase Friday morning, becoming
around 10 kt in the afternoon.

news.text:
.AVIATION /20Z MONDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
High pressure will remain offshore, while weak low pressure passes
to the south this afternoon and tonight. A cold front approaches
late tonight and remains in the vicinity through Tuesday morning.

Generally VFR for most terminals, except for eastern terminals such
as KISP and KGON, which may only improve to MVFR this afternoon with
brief breaks of VFR at times. MVFR to IFR conditions move back in
tonight, mainly for eastern terminals, with better conditions as you
head west. KJFK may see brief IFR conditions, while KEWR will likely
remain VFR.

As for precipitation, better chance for thunderstorms across the
western metro terminals (KEWR and KTEB) where there is a VCTS from
19Z-22Z this afternoon. Thunderstorms are more likely here, but
there is still some uncertainty with how far north they make it. If
they do move through, they will be associated with MVFR conditions
or lower. Less probable, but still at least 30% chance of seeing
thunder for KJFK and KLGA from 18Z today through 00Z tonight.

A S to SSE wind around 10 kt at the metro and coastal terminals, and
light inland, though winds may vary from SE to SW through early this
afternoon. Winds become light and variable once again tonight.
Gusts of 15 to around 20 kt are possible at some terminals
today, likely ending before 00Z tonight. A SW to WSW wind sets
up Tuesday at around 10 kt by mid to late morning.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

AMD likely overnight with changes in flight category in low
stratus/fog, mainly for KLGA and KEWR.

Any gusts likely end prior to 00Z this evening.

.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z TUESDAY THROUGH FRIDAY...

Tuesday afternoon: VFR, except MVFR or lower in afternoon showers
and tstms especially from the NYC metros north/west. Gusty winds
also possible in stronger storms.

Wednesday through Friday: Afternoon and evening showers/tstms
possible each day, with brief MVFR or IFR conditions.

Saturday: Mainly VFR. A slight chance for showers and an isolated
thunderstorm with MVFR or lower conditions.

approaches late tonight and remains in the vicinity through
the TAF period.

IFR all night KWER may only briefly see MVFR.

thunderstorms return Tuesday afternoon with some uncertainty in
exact timing and coverage. Kept PROB30 for now.

wind sets up Tuesday at around 10 kt by mid to late morning.
Given the nearby front there is more uncertainty than usual with
wind direction starting Tuesday afternoon.
